<findings>
<finding task="2"><quote>Files uploaded on the freeze date itself (UTC) are included.</quote><plan>return f'{self.freeze:%Y-%m-%d}T00:00:00Z'</plan><fix>R2.1 sets the cutoff to 00:00:00Z on the day after the freeze date. Make `cutoff` return `(freeze + 1 day)T00:00:00Z`. Change `test_cutoff_is_midnight_utc_on_the_freeze_date` to expect `2026-10-20T00:00:00Z` and `2027-01-01T00:00:00Z`. Change the `outputs` test and the `bump` test (`'2026-11-03T00:00:00Z'`) the same way. Rewrite the `uv.toml` comment to say that files uploaded on the freeze date are included. The `late_pins` test in Task 5 and the `uv_run_argv`, `run_suites` and drift expectations that spell the cutoff also follow the new value.</fix></finding>
<finding task="0"><quote>`exclude-newer` set to the RFC 3339 timestamp of 00:00:00Z on the day after the freeze date</quote><plan>The cutoff falls at the start of the freeze date, so every `bump` or `verify` run on that date resolves the same files, however late in the day it runs.</plan><fix>Restate the Freeze constraint and the Labels entry for "cutoff" as 00:00:00Z on the day after the freeze date. Drop the sentence that justifies the start-of-day cutoff. As written, `bump` (default: today) would exclude every file uploaded today.</fix></finding>
<finding task="0"><quote>It shadows the root date under `skills/`, so a skill script that a user runs floats within its floors (D8), whatever the path form</quote><plan>Every task's requirements include this section.</plan><fix>Add the required `## Review Focus` section after Global Constraints. List the five most likely untested failures, for example: a user running a skill script by real path or through a symlink floats; a worktree without the files inherits the freeze date; a `--pin` of a non-gate package; a `bump --only`; and `check` with a cited name at a different precision. Give each line a test in the task whose code would fail.</fix></finding>
<finding task="0"><quote>Exact pins in one file, plus a separate drift run on the newest releases.</quote><plan>**Q1 to Q8** are the open questions in this plan.</plan><fix>The plan's Decisions section reuses the labels D1 to D8, which the spec already uses for the owner's design decisions, and the Labels section still says D1 to D8 mean the spec's decisions. Renumber the plan's log entries so they do not collide (for example PD1 to PD8). Also remove the contradiction between "open questions … answer at plan review" plus the handoff "The decisions that need you are Q1 to Q8" and the log that says the owner already approved every default. Remove the leftover "If the owner answered Q2 with the alternative" branches.</fix></finding>
<finding task="9"><quote>Each script's `requires-python` must match the Python floor in its `SKILL.md` `compatibility:` line.</quote><plan>- **D4** (owner, plan review, 2026-10-21): Q4. The floors rule fails when a script needs a higher Python than its skill promises or than the dev Python. A lower script floor passes. Applied in: Task 9.</plan><fix>This changes what the spec requires ("must match" becomes "must not exceed"), so it is a spec-level decision. Add an amendment task with an exact replace-this-with-that block for R4.1 item 4, tagged `(owner, plan 66, 2026-10-21)`. Log it as "Task 9 (spec amendment)".</fix></finding>
<finding task="12"><quote>`build/check_jax_examples.py` and its documented command: they install `stack('jax-cpu')` in place of `--with-requirements specs/verification/32-jax-cpu.txt`.</quote><plan>- Move: `specs/verification/32-jax-cpu.in` and `32-jax-cpu.txt` to `specs/verification/completed/`</plan><fix>No task modifies `build/check_jax_examples.py`, whose usage docstring and any remediation text still name the retired lock file. Add it to Task 12 or 13. Add a step that greps live files (`build/`, `skills/`, `CLAUDE.md`, `skills/deep-learning/references/frameworks.md`) for `32-jax-cpu` and points every remaining reader at `build/versions.toml` and the `run jax-cpu` runner form.</fix></finding>
<finding task="13"><quote>The JAX CPU examples must pass on it.</quote><plan>uv run python build/versions.py run jax-cpu -- python build/check_jax_examples.py skills/deep-learning/</plan><fix>The old command set `JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu`. The new command drops it, and so does the `jax cpu examples` step that `verify_steps` builds in Task 8. Keep `JAX_PLATFORMS=cpu` in the documented command. In Task 8, have that step set it in its environment, and add a test that asserts the variable is set.</fix></finding>
<finding task="13"><quote>Documented commands spell no interpreter or package version.</quote><plan>It removes the flag text from every live file that the lint reads and prints the changed files.</plan><fix>The sweep and the lint remove only interpreter flags. Add a step that greps the live files for package versions inside documented commands (for example `--with "arviz>=1.0"` or `--with 'pkg==X'` in the usage docstrings of `build/check_snippets.py` and other `build/*.py` files). Rewrite each one to the runner form or to a bare name.</fix></finding>
<finding task="11"><quote>The known stale citations are the Polars, Altair and plotly lines</quote><plan>| `recommend-visualization` "Polars 1.42" (five places) | `HISTORICAL` with the reason "verified on 1.42, not re-checked on 2.x", and a deferred item. The claims need real charts in four libraries |</plan><fix>The Altair 6.2 and plotly 6.8 citations stay in `[cited]` at their old values, so `check` stays silent. Yet the spec names them as stale (latest 6.3.0 and 7.1.0). Settle them explicitly: name them in the Task 11 table, and extend the deferred item's "Done when" to cover the Altair and plotly re-checks and the matching `[cited]` updates.</fix></finding>
<finding task="8"><quote>`drift` exits 0 when each gate passes on the latest versions, 1 when a gate fails, and 2 when it cannot resolve or reach the network.</quote><plan>            failed = run_steps(steps, root, {**os.environ, 'UV_NO_CONFIG': '1'}, runner)</plan><fix>A re-verify step that fails because uv cannot reach the network is counted as a gate failure, so `drift` exits 1. Distinguish network or resolve failures in the step runs (for example, uv's exit status or stderr), map them to exit 2 with the report stating which, and add a stub-uv test for that case.</fix></finding>
<finding task="0"><quote>The plan writes each test before its code (red, then green).</quote><plan>- [ ] **Step 3: Write the module.** Create `build/versions.py`.</plan><fix>The plan transcribes whole module bodies (`versions.py`, `versions_check.py`, the probe script and the edit scripts) and runs far beyond five times the spec's length. Replace each module body with the exact signatures (already in the Interfaces blocks), the pinned values and the tests. Keep code only for algorithms that the tests do not determine (the citation regex and judge rules, the cutoff, the rewrite rule). Also drop no-op edits, such as Task 7's replace of `test_container_compares_path_parts_not_string_prefixes` with identical text.</fix></finding>
